title: POST /api/auth/register — email/password registration
description: Implement user registration with email and password. Hash the password, create the user record, issue access + refresh tokens, and return the user profile.
acceptanceCriteria: Returns 400 if email format is invalid or password is < 8 characters
Password is hashed with bcrypt before storage
Returns 201 with { user: { id, email, name }, accessToken } and sets HttpOnly refresh token cookie

steps.details: In server/: npm install bcryptjs jsonwebtoken. npm install -D @types/bcryptjs @types/jsonwebtoken.

Create server/src/utils/jwt.ts with: signAccessToken(userId: string): string — signs JWT with JWT_SECRET, 15m expiry, { sub: userId }. signRefreshToken(userId: string): string — signs with JWT_REFRESH_SECRET, 30d expiry. verifyAccessToken(token: string): { sub: string } — throws on invalid. verifyRefreshToken(token): { sub: string }.

steps.description: Create Zod validation schema for registration
steps.details: Create server/src/validators/auth.ts with: registerSchema = z.object({ email: z.string().email().max(255), name: z.string().min(1).max(255), password: z.string().min(8).max(100) }).

Create server/src/routes/auth.ts. Implement POST / (mounted at /api/auth/register): 1) Validate body with registerSchema. 2) Check if email already exists in users table (return 409 if so). 3) Hash password: await bcrypt.hash(password, 12). 4) Insert user into users table. 5) Sign access token and refresh token. 6) Store bcrypt hash of refresh token in refresh_tokens table with expires_at = 30 days from now. 7) Set refresh token in HttpOnly cookie ('refreshToken', 30d, sameSite: 'lax'). 8) Return 201 with { user: { id, email, name }, accessToken }.

steps.description: Mount auth router in main index.ts
steps.details: In server/src/index.ts, import authRouter and mount: app.use('/api/auth', authRouter).

Use curl or Postman: POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/register with body {"email":"test@example.com","name":"Test","password":"password123"}. Verify 201 response with accessToken. Verify user exists in DB with hashed password. Try registering same email again — expect 409.

technicalNotes: Refresh token should be set as HttpOnly, Secure (in prod), SameSite=Lax cookie to prevent XSS theft
Use bcrypt cost factor 12 — good balance of security and performance
Return 409 Conflict (not 400) when email is already taken
